title: VANTA.
grab: 18 MG995 servos, an aluminium disc horn on every joint
Mech hull with a camera visor, bolted leg armour
Servos stay closed, nothing needs soldering
check: Legs, base and stiffeners: ggldnl / Hexapod-Hardware (CERN-OHL-W-2.0). Caps, alu-horn brackets, hull, armour, electronics and software: VANTA.

title: Three
rules.
grab: Red: the part you add in this step
Black halftone: parts already on the robot
Boxes point at the part they talk about
do: Centre every servo first
Before a horn goes on (step 4), and never turn a servo shaft by hand after that. It's how the legs end up straight.
Battery unplugged
Whenever you're wiring or screwing anything. Only plug it in when a step says so.
Snug, not tight
Screws into inserts or self-tap holes strip the plastic if you crank them. Stop when the part stops moving.
check: Tools: soldering iron with an insert tip (200 °C for PLA), 2.5mm hex key plus a long one for the hull, multimeter, flush cutters, zip ties, a small knife, CA glue or tape, grip tape, a laptop that can SSH into the Pi.

title: Printed
parts.
segments.sub: — black PLA, 15 plates; hull and logo from the COLOR file
check: Hardware: 44 M3 heat-set inserts · 100× M3×6 · 48× M3×8 · 110× M3×10 · 12 washers · 12× M2.5×6 · 4× M2×8 + nuts · 18 623ZZ bearings · 18 alu 25T disc horns · 6 grip-tape strips.

title: Fit test:
one joint.
segments.blurb: Plate 1 decides which servo cap size you print, so do it before the big plates.
grab: Plate 1: caps +0 … +3, bracket A femur/tibia, bracket B alu
do: Bearing into the cap
Press the bearing into the +0 cap's hex boss from the outside, flush.
Cap onto the servo
Slide the cap over the servo bottom, cable through the notch.
Disc horn on the spline
Horn screw in. Bracket B over the disc; turn the disc a tooth at a time until its 4 holes line up with B's 4 holes (25 teeth, 4 holes: one always lines up within 2°). 4× M3×6.
Swing bracket A round
Its boss into the bearing, 2× M3×10 through B into A's end (they self-tap). Axle: M3×10 through A's side.
Read the gap
Look at the gap between A's boss and the bearing.
check: Gap 0.3–1mm: print the +0 caps. ~1.5mm: +1. ~2.5mm: +2. ~3.5mm: +3. Won't close: stop and measure. (Gio's horns: +1.)

title: Heat-set
inserts.
segments.blurb: 44 inserts, four parts. Soldering iron with an insert tip, 200 °C for PLA. Snug, never tight.
grab: Base, 6 femurs, 6 coxa bracket As, electronics plate
do: Base: 16
12 in the outer servo-tab holes underneath, 4 in the columns on top.
Femurs: 2 each
The two holes at the knee end of every femur.
Coxa bracket A: 2 each
The two holes in the end face, where bracket B's screws land.
Electronics plate: 4
One in each post, for the Pi deck and the hull screws.
check: Every insert flush and square. Let the iron's heat do the work; never push hard.

title: Power on
the bench.
segments.blurb: The power chain first, on the table, with nothing expensive plugged in.
grab: 20A SBEC, XL4015 buck, Wago connectors, 16AWG wire
do: Wire the power chain
Battery → fuse → switch → Wagos. The SBEC feeds the servos, the buck feeds the Pi.
Set the buck
Nothing on its output: adjust it with the multimeter to 5 V before the Pi ever sees it.
Alarm on the balance lead
Plug the LiPo alarm onto the balance connector so a low cell can't sneak past you.
check: Switch off and battery unplugged before anything else gets wired.

title: Reset all 18
servos to zero.
segments.blurb: Every servo goes to its zero (centre) position before any horn goes on. This is what makes the legs come out straight.
do: Wire the Pi to both PCA boards
4 jumpers each, like the picture in the guide.
Plug in the servos
ch0–8 of each board, brown wire to the board's outer edge.
Run center_servos
Switch on, SSH in, run python tools/center_servos.py. Every servo jumps to zero (centre) and holds there.
Mark the splines
Ctrl+C, switch off. A pen dot on each spline, facing up.
Turned a shaft by accident?
Plug that servo back in and run the script again before its horn goes on.
check: Every servo moved once and stopped; all 18 dots face the same way.
From here on, don't turn any servo shaft by hand: steps 8–11 rely on it.

title: Caps on
all servos.
segments.blurb: Same as the fit test, now for the rest. The hex boss is the outside of the cap.
do: Bearing into every cap
Press it into the hex boss from the outside, flush with the face.
Cap over the servo bottom
Cable through the notch.
Loose cap?
A wrap of tape on the servo fixes it.
check: The bearing turns freely with a finger and the cap doesn't rotate on the servo.

title: Coxa servos
into the base.
segments.blurb: Upside down: output shaft pointing at the floor, cap on top.
do: Turn the base over
Push each servo up through its pocket from below, cap first, until the tabs sit flat.
Outer tabs only
Toward the leg: M3×6 + washer into the inserts. The inner tabs wait for step 7.
check: All six output shafts face down, centred in the pocket.

title: Bottom stiffeners,
battery mount.
segments.blurb: The stiffeners clamp the inner servo tabs and hold the battery mount. They're not optional.
do: Battery mount under the middle
Its 4 corner ears go between the base and the stiffeners.
Stiffeners on
Over the inner servo tabs and the ears.
Through the counterbores, stiffener and tab into the base (they self-tap).
Through the stiffener corners and the battery ears.
Battery in
Velcro strap through the slots. Leave it unplugged.
check: Press on each coxa servo: nothing wobbles. The battery mount doesn't rattle.

title: Coxa
joints.
segments.blurb: Each leg's first joint. The servo is fixed, the bracket swings.
grab: Per leg: bracket A coxa, bracket B alu, 1 alu disc horn
do: Disc on the spline

Horn screw in. Bracket B over the disc; turn the disc a tooth at a time until its 4 holes line up with B's 4 holes (25 teeth, 4 holes: one always lines up within 2°). 4× M3×6. Set it so B points straight out from the body.
Bracket A over the top
Its boss on the cap's bearing.
A to B, then the axle
2× M3×8 through B's counterbores into A's inserts. Axle: M3×10.
check: Each bracket points straight out from the body.

title: Femur
frames.
segments.blurb: Each femur carries two servos: the femur servo and the tibia servo.
grab: Per leg: 1 femur (2 inserts in), 2 capped servos
do: Both servos in, cap first
From the insert face. The tabs rest on the frame.
Shafts on the same side
Both output shafts on the same side of the frame.
Eight screws
The two knee-end holes have inserts: M3×6. The other six self-tap: M3×8.
check: Both shafts on the same side, both caps poking out the other side.

title: Femur
joints.
segments.blurb: The femur bracket bolts to the coxa bracket. This time the servo body swings, not the bracket.
grab: Per leg: bracket A femur/tibia, bracket B alu, alu disc horn, the femur frame
do: Femur frame level
Horn screw in. Bracket B over the disc; turn the disc a tooth at a time until its 4 holes line up with B's 4 holes (25 teeth, 4 holes: one always lines up within 2°). 4× M3×6.
A around the servo
Boss on the cap bearing, 2× M3×10 through B into A, M3×10 axle.
Back to back with the coxa A
4× M3×10 from inside the coxa bracket. The heads sink into its counterbores.
check: With everything centred the femur sticks straight out, level.

title: Tibia joints,
grip feet.
segments.blurb: Last joint, then grip tape on the tip. No TPU feet in this build.
grab: Per leg: bracket A femur/tibia, bracket B alu, alu disc horn, 1 tibia
4× M3×6, 7× M3×10, a strip of grip tape
do: Same U round the outer servo
Axle included. Set the horn so the tibia points straight down when the femur is level.
Tibia onto A's 4-hole face
4× M3×10 through the tibia's counterbores (they self-tap into A).
Grip tape
Wrap it round the bottom 25mm of the tip, overlapping on the inner face. Trim the end.
check: Femur level, tibia straight down, tip wrapped tight.

title: Check the legs,
fit the armour.
segments.blurb: Centred pose first, then the armour. The armour is cosmetic: glue or tape, no screws.
do: Check every leg
Coxa straight out, femur level, tibia straight down. A joint off: 4 horn screws out, next tooth that lines up, screws back.
Femur plates
One on each side rail, rib and bolts outward, the cut corner toward the knee. Glue only where the plate touches the rail.
Shin plates
On the outer face of each tibia, flush with the bend at the top.
Move each leg by hand
Through its walking range, not to the end stops: nothing rubs.
check: All six legs match. Small errors (under 2°) get trimmed in software later.

title: Electronics
plate.
segments.blurb: Top stiffeners, the plate, then the boards on it.
grab: Top stiffeners, electronics plate (4 inserts in the posts)
do: Top stiffeners on
The 4 base columns go through their corner notches; the stiffeners rest on the coxa servos.
Plate on top
4× M3×6 into the column inserts. It clamps the stiffeners.
PCA boards on the bosses
Servo headers facing out. Front board = PCA #1, rear = PCA #2. Label them.
Zip ties
The buck to the rear slots, the SBEC to the front slots.
check: Nothing touches the coxa caps when you turn a leg by its bracket.

title: Power in
the robot.
segments.blurb: The bench chain from step 3 moves into the body. Battery still unplugged.
do: Battery lead to the switch
Through the fuse, then the switch where you can reach it from underneath.
Split at the Wagos
One pair to the SBEC in, one to the buck in. Keep the runs short and tied down.
SBEC out to both PCAs
V+ and GND on each board's power terminals.
Buck out to the Pi
5 V to pins 2 and 4, GND to pins 6 and 9. Leave about 15cm of slack: the fans join here in step 18.
check: Metered with the switch on and no boards plugged: buck at 5 V, nothing warm. Then off, battery out.

title: Servo
leads.
segments.blurb: Three servos per leg, one channel each. The tibia servos need the 30cm extensions.
do: Extensions on the tibia servos
Theirs are the leads that don't reach.
Route along the leg
Down the femur rail into the body, with slack at every joint through its full swing.
Plug in by leg
Brown wire to the board's outer edge. Keep the step 4 channel order: front board PCA #1, rear PCA #2.
Label and tie
Mark each plug with its leg and joint; zip-tie the bundles to the plate slots.
check: Swing every leg through its range by the bracket: no lead goes tight, nothing hangs into a joint.

title: Pi deck
and camera.
segments.blurb: The deck sits on the four posts. No screws yet: the hull bolts through it in step 18.
grab: Pi deck, Pi 4 (SD card in), camera + ribbon
do: Pi on the bosses
USB ports to the back. Camera on the front wall, lens through the hole.
Ribbon in
Into the Pi's camera port, blue tab toward the USB ports.
Jumpers down the left slot
Pi to both PCAs (step 4 picture). Buck output to pins 2, 4 and 6, 9.
Deck onto the posts
The servo plugs come up through the two long windows. Lay their wires flat before the Pi goes over them.
check: Ribbon not pinched, jumpers not tight, no servo wire under tension, nothing hanging into the legs.

title: First
power-up.
segments.blurb: Hold it up off the table the first time, legs in the air.
grab: The finished robot (hull off), charged battery
A laptop on the same Wi-Fi
do: Battery in, alarm on, switch on
The Pi's light blinks, the boards' LEDs light.
SSH in
i2cdetect -y 1 and i2cdetect -y 3 both show 40.
Throttle check
vcgencmd get_throttled says 0x0.
Centre again
python tools/center_servos.py: every servo goes to zero, the step 12 pose.
Wrong way, or hits something?
Ctrl+C. It's on the wrong channel.
check: All 18 servos hold the zero pose; nothing buzzes hard or gets hot.
Shut the Pi down (sudo shutdown now) before switching off. Stop at the LiPo alarm (3.5V per cell).

title: Mech
hull.
segments.blurb: Hides everything. The legs never touch it: it sits inside the old shell's envelope.
do: Leads through the slots
Six slots along the bottom edge, one leg pair per slot. Fan leads into the buck's OUT terminals.
Lower it straight down
The camera lens in the visor at the front.
Four bosses on the deck
4× M3×10 down through the round ports in the armour, through the deck into the post inserts.
Snug only
Battery and switch stay reachable from underneath.
check: Run tools/center_servos.py again and wiggle each leg through its range: no leg touches the hull. Camera sees through the visor.

title: Made
by Gio.
grab: Keep a spare MG995 or two on hand
check: Legs, base and stiffeners: ggldnl / Hexapod-Hardware, CERN-OHL-W-2.0. Everything else: VANTA. Keep the notice and the source files with the build.
